_README: WORKED EXAMPLE -- this is ../config.json with every placeholder filled in, for the Sandy Cheeks profile -- a field research engineer from an isolated marine station, targeting industry hardware engineering AND research science equally, job-hunting in Texas. That profile and its SCORING.md were GENERATED BY /jobscan-setup from examples/material/, not written by hand; this config's prescreen was then merged to cover both directions. Copy it over ../config.json to see the pipeline run end to end, then replace the companies and prescreen terms with your own. EVERY SOURCE BELOW WAS VERIFIED with `python3 jobscan.py --check` on 2026-08-24; re-run it before trusting a scan, because boards move. Note what the template cannot show you: the prescreen lists here are the result of running once and reading the output, not of guessing well. Regions live in this file under `regions`, so copying it over ../config.json is all the demo needs.

companies._comment: Austin humanoid robotics. The largest board here (~78 roles) and the closest match to this profile: actuators, control, test engineering, field robotics.
Austin service robotics, ~16 roles. Small board, high signal density -- judge a source by its Apply count, not its role count.

Austin, 3D-printed construction. VERIFIED HEALTHY BUT CURRENTLY EMPTY: the token resolves and the endpoint returns 200 with zero open roles. That is a real state, not a failure, and --check prints `ok` for it either way -- exactly the case PLATFORMS.md warns about. Keep it and watch the count rather than deleting it.
Dallas. De-extinction and conservation biotech -- included because it is the one employer here where the marine-biology half of this profile is the point rather than a curiosity.
Austin. Kept mainly as the worked `lever` example -- the fit is weak and its Skip reasons are what tuned `discovery_block` below.

Colorado rocket propulsion, ~99 roles. OUT OF REGION ON PURPOSE: it shows what an out-of-region board looks like in a --check (healthy count, almost nothing surviving the location filter). Delete it unless you would relocate.

San Antonio. The worked example of covering an employer whose own portal resists scripting -- and of the SILENT ZERO. `location` and `category` take repeated values with OR semantics, so one query covers the region. But USAA's Muse postings do not carry the categories this search would ask for: filtering on them drops 100% of its roles and the source returns 0 while --check still prints `ok`. So this source deliberately has NO `categories` key. Verified 2026-08-24: company only = 88, company + these locations = 19, company + locations + Science/Data/Software categories = 0. Always run that three-way test before trusting a Muse count.

PROMOTED FROM DISCOVERY 2026-08-24. Surfaced by the himalayas sweep as a remote-US GNC role; the thematic fit is the strongest in this config (they build inflatable space habitats, this profile built and lived in a pressurised one). Board is 169 roles and Colorado-centric, so most are dropped by the Texas location filter -- it is here for the remote postings and for the day the relocation question gets asked. Tenant found from the careers page: the myworkdayjobs URL is embedded in the HTML, which is the cheapest way to get tenant+site. WATCH THIS SOURCE: on its first run 24 of its 25 candidates carried Workday's vague '2 Locations', which location_ok() keeps by design (step 1, the documented soft spot -- dropping them would lose real multi-site roles). Sierra Space is Broomfield CO, so most of those 24 are almost certainly Colorado. It is kept because the habitat fit is worth a relocation conversation, but if you will not leave Texas this is the first source to delete.

PROMOTED FROM DISCOVERY 2026-08-24 (Senior Microwave Research Scientist, remote-US). Quantum hardware -- cryogenics, vacuum, precision instrumentation, which is adjacent to the habitat and instrumentation strands. 103 roles, mostly Pleasanton CA and College Park MD.

PROMOTED FROM DISCOVERY 2026-08-24. Warehouse-inventory drones -- small board (15 roles), robotics-hardware shop. The kind of employer nobody would have thought to track, which is exactly what the discovery budget is for.

PROMOTED FROM DISCOVERY 2026-08-24. Robotics (Robotics AI Engineer, Electrical Engineer Robotics on the board). 20 roles, San Francisco. NOTE ON THE TOKEN: `menlo` is right, but two other promotions from this same run were NOT -- ashby `clera` returns 300 marketing and intern roles for an unrelated company, and ashby `foundation` is a four-person design shop, neither of them the employer discovery had surfaced. Verify the ROWS, not just that the token resolves.

PROMOTED FROM _manual 2026-08-24 -- it had been recorded as 'NO ROUTE FOUND' and that was wrong. The board is ClearCompany, injected by a script tag on the careers page carrying the siteId. TWO reasons the original fingerprint missed it: `clearcompany` was not in the grep pattern list (the same omission that made a Paradox site look like a custom JS portal), and that script tag has an UNQUOTED src, so a regex expecting src="..." could not match it either. 169 roles, full descriptions inline (median ~4,900 chars), no key, no pagination params needed -- though the adapter pages anyway because the single 1.2MB response intermittently truncates. Cedar Park and Briggs TX: the best-located employer in this config for this profile, and the one whose locations exposed the missing ' tx' region token.

Company-less sweep across every employer The Muse indexes in these regions -- 6,662 roles at last check. This is the general-purpose half of the config and is worth keeping whatever you are looking for: it is how employers you had never heard of reach the shortlist. Titles are the only lever; The Muse has no free-text search parameter. Category names must match exactly: `Operations` returns 0 (the real name is `Business Operations`) and `Engineering` does not exist (it is `Science and Engineering`). CATEGORIES CHANGED 2026-08-24 when the profile gained a research direction: 'Education' added (verified 11,639 results) because academic and institute roles are categorised there; 'Data and Analytics' and 'Software Engineering' removed after measuring that they tripled the sweep to 3,092 with product and business analytics. Also verified: 'Research' and 'Operations' return ZERO and are not real Muse category names -- The Muse CANNOT be filtered for research roles, so titles do it.

Remote-only aggregator -- the second discovery source, covering a population The Muse structurally cannot: remote-first employers have no office to be indexed against. USES THE SEARCH ENDPOINT because `queries` is set, and that is the whole difference between this source being worth having and not. Verified 2026-08-24, same budget both ways: WITHOUT queries (browse firehose) 400 fetched -> 265 past locations -> 1 past prescreen. WITH these queries 283 fetched -> 283 past locations -> 60 past prescreen, 189 distinct employers, median description 4,776 chars. `q` is FUZZY and more words BROADEN rather than narrow (q=engineer gives 31 hits, q=mechanical engineer gives 147), so write specific phrases and accept the overlap -- rows are deduped by guid across queries. Cost is one request per 20 rows: 8 queries x 3 pages = up to 24 requests. QUERIES REBALANCED 2026-08-24: four hardware phrases and four research phrases, matching the profile's two equally-weighted directions.

prescreen._comment: Title-level gate before the LLM scoring pass. `block` rejects outright; a title then needs >= min_signal hits from `signal`. Discovery sources additionally must clear discovery_block and match discovery_signal, because an open Texas sweep is overwhelmingly healthcare, finance and oilfield services. LIVE EXAMPLE OF THE TUNING LOOP: the first run of this config let 'Field Service Technician' and 'Reservoir Engineer' through -- `field` and `engineer` are too generic on a Texas board -- and let a wall of nursing titles through discovery because 'Clinical Research Scientist' matches `scientist`. A second pass caught more: `intern$` (anchored) missed 'Robotics Software Intern - Real-Time Controls', and `manager,` missed 'Senior Manager of Mechanical Engineering' -- both needed unanchored variants. The fix throughout was to add to `block` and `discovery_block`, NOT to narrow `signal`: narrowing `signal` would also have dropped 'Research Scientist, Habitats', which is the single best-fitting title this config has produced. A THIRD PASS after promoting discovery finds: Sierra Space alone contributed 25 candidates, ten of them titled '(Clearance Required)'. 'No security clearance' is an explicit hard gap in profile.md, so those roles are unreachable by definition and were pure noise -- `clearance` and friends are now blocked. This is the rule about never crediting a listed gap, applied at the prescreen instead of waiting for the scorer to spend effort skipping them one by one. A FOURTH PASS after adding Firefly (169 roles, the biggest tracked board): trade and management titles leaked -- 'Aerospace Welder III', 'Spacecraft Test Technician IV', 'Quality Assurance Manager - Spacecraft'. `manager,` and `manager of` did not catch 'Manager -' or a trailing 'Manager', so `\bmanager\b` replaces the guesswork; `welder` and `\btechnician\b` cover the trades. All three are wrong-LEVEL rather than wrong-field, which the rubric treats as a bigger negative than mismatch upward. FIFTH PASS, 2026-08-24: profile.md was regenerated by /jobscan-setup and now targets industry hardware engineering AND research science equally, so this gate carries TWO vocabularies. Research terms were added to `signal` and `discovery_signal`; the cost is that bare 'Research Scientist' titles reveal nothing about domain, so an AI/ML research population arrives that no title-level rule can separate. That was measured on the two sweeps alone: 29 candidates of which 17 were noise in three clean buckets (8 AI/ML research, 6 power-plant instrumentation & controls, 2 silicon/RF). Blocking those buckets took it to 12. Five of the remaining 12 are still domain-ambiguous 'Research Scientist' rows and are DELIBERATELY LEFT IN -- blocking harder would cost real research roles, and reading requirements is the scorer's job, not the prescreen's. NOTE what is still absent from `signal` on purpose: a bare 'engineer' or bare 'scientist'. In a Texas sweep the first admits civil, project-controls and petroleum roles wholesale and the second admits the entire clinical research population. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY IN WHAT IS BLOCKED: `clearance` is here because it is a HARD GATE -- no clearance means the role is unobtainable however good the fit. `fea`, `cfd`, `cad`, `plm` and `gd&t` are deliberately ABSENT even though all of them are listed gaps in profile.md, because they are LEARNABLE gaps: blocking them would delete roles that are otherwise strong fits, and the surrounding domain is what decides. See the 'learnable gap' section of SCORING.md.

_manual._comment: Companies with no first-party automated route, and what covers them instead. Record the exact endpoints that failed and how -- a 'no route' verdict is only as good as the specific thing that was tried, and re-testing one is cheap (/jobscan-connector). These are real findings from building this example config on 2026-08-24. ONE ENTRY LEFT THIS TABLE ON 2026-08-24: Firefly Aerospace, which said 'NO ROUTE FOUND'. It is a ClearCompany board and always was. That is the third time in this project's history a 'nothing works' verdict was simply wrong -- re-test these before trusting them.
_manual.Southwest Research Institute: swri.org/careers fingerprints as no known platform -- the grep for the ~15 common ATS names returns nothing, so the careers page is a shell of some kind. Not on The Muse (total=0). NOT RE-TESTED beyond that; a genuinely good fit for this profile, so worth someone spending an hour on.
_manual.Most large Texas employers: Lockheed Martin, Texas Instruments, L3Harris, Jacobs, KBR, Halliburton, Baker Hughes and ExxonMobil ALL return total=0 on The Muse (verified 2026-08-24). The Muse is not a general fallback for Texas industrials the way it is for consumer tech -- go to their own ATS or do without.
_manual.Applied Materials: Surfaced by discovery (via The Muse) as Mechanical Engineer III, Robotics. Its own careers page fingerprints as no known ATS platform -- the grep for the ~15 common names returns nothing. NOT promoted: it is already reachable through the Muse sweep, so a first-party connector would add nothing but a second copy of the same rows.
_manual.Blue River Technology: Surfaced by discovery (via himalayas), scored 5. Its careers page fingerprints as no known platform; it is a John Deere subsidiary, so its real board is probably Deere's Workday. NOT PURSUED -- one mid-scoring role did not justify the hunt. Revisit if it reappears.

regions._comment: Region tokens for the location filter, matched case-insensitively. DESIGN PRINCIPLE: ' tx' (leading space, no trailing) does most of the work -- it matches 'Austin, TX', 'US, TX, Houston' and 'Briggs TX' alike, so it covers any posting that names the state in any format. City tokens are therefore only needed for postings that OMIT the state ('Austin', 'Greater Houston Area'). Consequently, bare city tokens are included ONLY where the name is unambiguous nationally. arlington, frisco, georgetown, san marcos, pasadena, irving, kyle and katy are deliberately absent: each exists in another state, ' tx' already catches the Texas ones, and a bare token would silently admit Arlington VA, Frisco CO and Georgetown KY.
